answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable bond before trading, like a terrace that admits one stall per deposit. The bond stays locked through a long voyage of verified transactions and is slashed if the same operator is caught running duplicate identities, while an honest agent recovers its single bond. Forging thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of bonds, so attack cost grows linearly, whereas a real agent pays once, and an ivory reputation badge alone, without a bond at stake, proves nothing.
